Table of Contents
1. Introduction
1.1 Purpose of this report

This report records tool-based testing and quality evaluation of the LegalEase AI system developed for SE3090. It preserves the SE3110 test plan, case designs, defects and contribution disclosures while distinguishing actual execution evidence from historical claims and unresolved requirements.

Publication revision: 8 October 2026 (Asia/Colombo). Approved tested source 05359214df52, including fixes f360e4ac21f1, is published on Wishwa2002/Intelligent-legal-service, branch se3110-qmse-testing. Original development history is preserved; no deployment or submission occurred. GitHub CI did not trigger for this branch. Available SE3090 Version 3.0 reference reviewed; formal approval unconfirmed. Original, 51-page and pre-publication 60-page reports are preserved.

Repository provenance: Wishwa2002/Intelligent-legal-service is the original group development repository. Its main/develop/feature histories retain recorded authors and dates; the new testing branch preserves that ancestry. Jeyamdev/legalease-ai is the deployment repository used for hosting and recent local QMSE preparation. It is not the original group-history repository. Eleven newer deployment-only commits were excluded because they were outside the verified baseline.

2. Test Plan
2.1 Objectives
Verify that the key features of all four business components behave as specified (FR-01 to FR-16).
Demonstrate at least one complete integrated workflow across Flutter, the .NET API, PostgreSQL, the Python AI mesh and the React clerk portal.
Measure performance against NFR-01 (API p95 < 200 ms, AI < 1.5 s) and verify security controls (JWT, RBAC, BCrypt, prompt-injection defence).
Record actual results, mark every test Passed or Failed, log defects, fix important ones and retest.

Keep reusable automated test scripts in the published testing branch and retain native reports, screenshots and final documents in the separately supplied evidence package so results can be reproduced and explained.

Each case records design, expected outcome, actual observation and evidence. VERIFIED means a scoped fresh result supported by an execution artifact; FAILED means an observed defect or a report expectation conflict (identified explicitly). BLOCKED and NOT EXECUTED mean no valid execution result. H/U means HISTORICAL/UNVERIFIED: the original reported result is retained as history, not a current PASS. Current automation-case names and exact setups are in qmse-output/completion-20261008/test-results/case-verification.json. Fixture dates such as 2030-01-14 are synthetic inputs, not execution dates.

7. Non-Functional Test Analysis
7.1 Performance

A controlled k6 2.3.0 retest used two virtual users for 15 seconds against the actual ASP.NET Staging API and isolated PostgreSQL 18. It completed 30 iterations and 120 requests with 0% HTTP errors and 7.803 requests/second. Search p50/p95/average: 3.487/5.679/3.724 ms; details: 2.134/3.528/2.277 ms; appointments GET: 1.500/3.585/1.694 ms; documentation GET: 15.475/20.966/15.831 ms. All measured p95 values meet 200 ms in this small synthetic local scope; no hosted or transactional booking load acceptance is inferred.

The original login p95 of 180 ms has no measurement artifact. Login latency was not benchmarked in the new run. DEF-07 is a monitoring observation, not a demonstrated breach of the 200 ms budget. Hash cost and latency should be measured with the actual configured deployment.

One live Gemini request, retries disabled, returned provider ServerError 504 after 29.326 seconds. No successful output/token usage or verified pricing was returned, so estimated cost is unavailable and the 1.5-second successful-response NFR is BLOCKED. Only one of eight authorised calls was attempted; testing stopped on provider failure. Prior mock-gateway timings remain historical mock measurements.

The initial real PostgreSQL k6 run exposed appointment-list HTTP 500 due to missing migration columns and failed its error threshold. The additive migration fixed the isolated schema, and the retained retest has zero HTTP errors. Read-only endpoint timings do not measure transactional booking throughput. Concurrent booking is separately verified with real PostgreSQL service tests.
7.2 Security

Expanded OWASP ZAP 2.17.0 inspection used 15 deliberate loopback requests to the actual Staging API/PostgreSQL environment, with passive scanning and finite manual authentication/injection probes. Final native report: nine Low X-Content-Type-Options missing instances and one Informational authentication-identification instance. The header finding remains OPEN. The earlier application-error alert associated with schema HTTP 500 is absent after repair; this does not prove absence of other vulnerabilities. No automated active scan, spider or production traffic was used. Genuine upload/JWT/role tests and SQL-like input probes complement the scan.

Git publication security note: GitHub push output reported nine default-branch Dependabot alerts (seven high, two moderate); no authenticated advisory review or remediation was performed. These are separate from local ZAP findings. A database-connection artifact was also identified in pre-existing public main history and is absent from the tested tree. Its contents/credential-like filename are excluded from deliverables; the group must review rotation/removal with repository owners. No history rewrite was authorised.
7.3 Reliability and recovery

Actual PostgreSQL attachment commit failure rolls back the file insert and request-status change. An explicit caller transaction rolls back request creation after failed attachment validation. Separate create/upload HTTP operations remain non-atomic as a group; no new batch operation was invented. Mocked timeout recovery and direct booking without AI still pass at their documented service scope.
7.4 Usability and compatibility

Flutter SDK recovery enabled a genuine web build and actual browser workflow, including upload and synchronized completion. The 49 existing Flutter unit/widget cases also pass. React integration now uses the correct clerk profile ID; two added browser regressions pass and the real queue/review was executed. Physical Android/iOS-device compatibility, accessibility conformance and complete cross-platform equivalence remain unverified.
8. Agentic AI Testing and Evaluation

All 102 final Python deterministic/mocked tests pass. A versioned synthetic Golden Case dataset now records fixtures, expected outputs and success criteria. Three GC-03 deterministic checklist subcases produce the expected missing-document/ready statuses; the GC-04 subcase demonstrates sanitizer isolation only, not live refusal or a universal disclaimer. GC-01 live classification returned provider 504; live GC-02–04 were not attempted after failure. No historical 98.9% mean or original case accuracy is certified.
